ordered_diagnoses: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead
salient_findings: Arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
Dermoscopic examination revealed short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of his forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

shortlist: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive direct immunofluorescence and granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in dermal blood vessels

shortlist.label: Lichen planopilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead

shortlist.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
shortlist.why_kept: Linear furrow on the left side of the forehead and localized hair loss on the scalp

shortlist.label: Pseudopelade of Brocq
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple, small, asymptomatic, depressed skin lesions with hair loss on the scalp

shortlist.label: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead

shortlist.label: Graham-Little syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead

shortlist.label: Alopecia areata
shortlist.why_kept: Localized hair loss on the scalp and presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination

shortlist.label: Linear scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Linear furrow on the left side of the forehead and localized hair loss on the scalp

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove with localized linear hair loss, combined with histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and positive direct immunofluorescence with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen, is most consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Lichen planopilaris
rejected.why: While lichen planopilaris can cause scarring alopecia, the presence of positive direct immunofluorescence and the specific pattern of hair loss are more suggestive of discoid lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
rejected.why: Frontal fibrosing alopecia typically presents with band-like hair loss along the frontal hairline, which does not match the patient's presentation of an arc-shaped lesion on the left side of the forehead and scalp.

rejected.label: Pseudopelade of Brocq
rejected.why: Pseudopelade of Brocq is a non-inflammatory condition that does not typically present with the same level of inflammation or positive immunofluorescence findings as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution
rejected.why: This condition is a type of scarring alopecia that follows a pattern of hair loss, but the patient's presentation and histopathologic findings are more consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Graham-Little syndrome
rejected.why: Graham-Little syndrome is a rare condition characterized by scarring alopecia, but it typically presents with a more widespread and symmetrical pattern of hair loss, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Alopecia areata
rejected.why: Alopecia areata is a non-scarring form of hair loss that does not typically present with the same level of inflammation or scarring as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Linear scleroderma
rejected.why: Linear scleroderma can cause skin lesions and hair loss, but the patient's presentation and histopathologic findings are more consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.
